title: Interplay of Magnetic Order, Structural Stability, and Orbital Ordering in BaFe2X3 (X = S and Se)
authors: Kunihiko Yamauchi, Takuya Aoyama, Kenya Ohgushi
abstract: BaFe2X3 (X= S and Se) are quasi-one-dimensional Mott insulators with a ladder structure that exhibit Stripe- and Block-type antiferromagnetic order, respectively. The ladder arrangement of Fe atoms and strong electron correlations give rise to rich magnetic and orbital phenomena, including pressure-induced superconductivity and orbital-selective electronic states. Both compounds also show resistivity anomalies above the Neel temperature, suggesting that orbital degrees of freedom play an important role in their electronic properties. To clarify the interplay among magnetic order, structural stability, orbital ordering, and transport properties, we performed resistivity measurements and first-principles calculations for BaFe2S3 and BaFe2Se3, systematically comparing candidate magnetic and crystal structures. We find that the magnetic configuration strongly influences the stable crystal structure, orbital ordering, and transport anisotropy, providing a microscopic understanding of the contrasting electronic properties of the two compounds.
summary: This work investigates how magnetic order dictates structural stability and orbital arrangement in the Mott insulators BaFe2X3. By combining DFT calculations with experimental measurements, the authors demonstrate that symmetry breaking, particularly in the Block-B state of BaFe2Se3, enhances orbital polarization, offering a microscopic understanding of the contrasting electronic behaviors of the two compounds.
main_problem: The study aims to clarify the complex interplay among magnetic order, structural stability, orbital ordering, and transport properties in the quasi-one-dimensional Mott insulators, BaFe2X3 (X = S and Se).
main_result: The magnetic configuration dictates the stable crystal structure and orbital ordering, with the Block-B state in BaFe2Se3 showing enhanced orbital polarization due to a cooperative Jahn–Teller-like distortion.
method: The research combines experimental resistivity measurements with first-principles calculations (DFT+U) to systematically compare candidate magnetic and crystal structures.
model_or_system: The physical system is the compound BaFe2X3 (X=S and Se), which possesses a ladder structure and exhibits rich magnetic and orbital phenomena. The calculations model various magnetic states (Néel, Stripe, Block) and associated crystal symmetries.
key_observables: Resistivity anomalies, relative energies ($\Delta E$), band gaps ($E_{	ext{gap}}$), and orbital polarization patterns visualized via partial charge densities.
important_parameters: The Hubbard U parameter (e.g., U=3 eV) is crucial for treating correlation effects; temperature ($T$) and magnetic ordering wavevectors ($\mathbf{q}$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on DFT+U approximations and assume that structural stability is governed by the minimization of total energy across different magnetic/structural phases.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures in different symmetries (Cmcm, Pnma, Pmn21), temperature dependence of resistivity, and visualizations of orbital ordering patterns associated with various magnetic states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the structural implications of different magnetic orders (Néel, Stripe, Block) for both BaFe2S3 and BaFe2Se3, using DFT calculations to determine the most stable configuration and correlating this with observed transport anomalies.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between lattice distortions (structural stability) and electronic degrees of freedom (orbital ordering) is a hallmark of strongly correlated electron systems, providing insights into mechanisms beyond simple magnetic ordering.
